last_message:
I implemented `can_place_order` in `larder/limits.py`, following the spec in `docs/features/ordering-limits.md`. A household is all the members registered at the same address, and it can hold at most 2 open pantry orders, counted across all its members. The function adds up the open orders of everyone at the member's address and allows a new order only while that total is below 2. The member is counted even if they're missing from `members`, and never counted twice.

I also added `tests/test_limits.py` with four tests: below the limit, at the limit, orders from two members of the same household adding up, and orders from other households not counting. All 6 tests pass (`python3 -m pytest -q`).

One thing to know: addresses are matched exactly as stored, so "1 Elm St" and "1 Elm Street" count as different households. The spec doesn't say how addresses should be normalised, so I didn't guess. If addresses aren't already cleaned up when members register, one family could get around the limit by writing its address slightly differently. That might be worth listing under a `Known limits` section on the ordering-limits page.
